---
title: "Module 10 — Testing"
---

## Goal

Test the system at two layers that serve different purposes.

```
             Rust core
             ▲       ▲
             │       │
        Rust tests   PyO3
                     │
                     ▼
                  Python API
                     ▲
                     │
                  pytest
```

## Layer 1 — Rust tests (canonical behaviour)

```bash
cargo test
```

These tests exercise the domain logic **without** Python in the loop.

They answer: “Does the kernel implement the rules correctly?”

## Layer 2 — Python tests (public contract)

```bash
pytest tests/python
```

These tests exercise the exposed API the way a Python application would use it.

They answer: “Does the package we ship behave as documented for Python callers?”

## Why both are required

| Layer        | Protects against |
|--------------|------------------|
| Rust tests   | Logic regressions inside the kernel |
| Python tests | Binding mistakes, conversion bugs, packaging gaps |

A pure Rust test suite cannot catch a broken `#[pyfunction]` annotation.  
A pure Python test suite is a slow way to debug a pure domain-logic error.

## Exercise

1. Run `cargo test` and confirm the domain tests pass.
2. Run the Python test suite (see `kernel/tests/python/`).
3. Intentionally break one Rust invariant and observe which layer fails first.
